# 1st Script: Cleaning Up Raw Data

## Project question

**Question C, Species occurrence:** for selected taxa, where and when
were they recorded across OPIHI surveys, and how often were they
detected once sampling effort (number of quadrats) is accounted for?

*Primary metric (to be finalised):* detection frequency = quadrats where
the taxon was recorded / quadrats sampled, per site-visit, summarised by
site and year.

## Setup and load libraries

```{r setup}
# ---- Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Stops with the exact install command if anything is missing, so a new user
# knows what to do instead of hitting a cryptic error halfway through.
needed <- c(
  # data handling
  "tidyverse", "dplyr", "tidyr", "stringr", "stringi", "purrr", "readr",
  "tibble", "lubridate", "janitor",
  # reading Excel files
  "readxl", "cellranger", "tidyxl",
  # paths, reports and tables
  "here", "knitr", "gt", "webshot2",
  # plots
  "ggplot2", "patchwork",
  # maps
  "maps", "mapdata", "mapproj", "sf", "maptiles", "tidyterra",
  "tidygeocoder", "ggspatial", "leaflet", "leafpop"
)

missing <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  stop("Missing packages. Run this once, then re-run:\n  install.packages(c(",
       paste0('"', missing, '"', collapse = ", "), "))")
}

# Load libraries 
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
library(stringr)
library(maps)
library(mapdata)
library(mapproj)
library(leaflet)
library(sf)
library(maptiles)
library(tidyterra)
library(tidygeocoder)
library(ggspatial)
library(leafpop)
library(patchwork)
library(grid)
library(tidyxl)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(gt)
library(webshot2)

# ---- Project paths ----------------------------------------------------------
# Project layout (the top folder can have any name or location):
#   <project>/
#   ├── OPIHI.Rproj      marks the project root
#   ├── Data/
#   │   ├── Raw/         original Excel files, unedited, original names
#   │   └── Processed/   everything this code writes (CSV copies, master, logs)
#   │   └── Lookups/     editable site and taxon crosswalks (inputs)
#   │   ├── Algae/       algae origin lookup and team review file (inputs)
#   ├── Scripts/         this .qmd + the R function files sourced below
#   └── Outputs/          figures and tables for the report
# Nothing in Data/Raw/ is ever modified by this code.
#
# here::i_am() declares where THIS file sits inside the project. here::here()
# then builds every path from the project root, so the code runs unchanged on
# any computer, whether rendered, run chunk-by-chunk, or run from the console.
here::i_am("Scripts/FinalScript_GroupC.qmd")

RAW_DIR    <- here::here("Data", "Raw")
CSV_DIR    <- here::here("Data", "Processed", "raw_csv")
CLEAN_DIR  <- here::here("Data", "Processed")
OUTPUT_DIR <- here::here("Outputs")
ALGAE_DIR  <- here::here("Data", "Algae")
dir.create(CSV_DIR,    showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

source(here::here("Scripts", "helpers.R"))
source(here::here("Scripts", "import_legacy.R"))
source(here::here("Scripts", "import_modern.R"))
source(here::here("Scripts", "import_classroom.R"))
source(here::here("Scripts", "clean_build.R"))

# Editable lookup tables (inputs, not outputs): see section 6
site_xw  <- read_lookup(here::here("Data", "Lookups", "site_crosswalk.csv"))
taxon_xw <- read_lookup(here::here("Data", "Lookups", "taxon_crosswalk.csv"))

if (length(list_raw_xlsx(RAW_DIR)) == 0) {
  stop("No .xlsx files found in ", RAW_DIR,
       ". Put the original OPIHI Excel files there (see README).")
}
```

## 1. Raw data inventory

The datasheets come in four structural "families". Each family gets one
importer, rather than one per file.

| Family | Files | Layout | Resolution | Role |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| **A. Legacy blocks** | `OPIHI data 2004`–`2020` | Field-trip blocks side by side; taxa = rows, quadrats = columns | Quadrat | Primary source |
| **B. Modern row-per-quadrat** | 2024 datasheet, BIOL 499 2025, 2026 Longitudinal, RAW Mauliola 2026 | One row per quadrat; taxa = columns; Metadata tab | Quadrat | Primary source |
| **C. Classroom Field Study** | Field Study 2023, 2025, 2026 Waipuilani | Student-group columns; taxa = rows | Group totals | Kept, flagged `group_total`; not used for detection frequency |
| **D. Derived / compiled** | Reformated, Playing around 2022, Sandy Beach Only, Copy of 2024 | Trip totals, subsets, recalculations | Varies | Duplicates: used only to cross-check A and B |

```{r inventory}
inventory <- tibble(file = list_raw_xlsx(RAW_DIR, full.names = FALSE)) |>
  mutate(
    family = case_when(
      str_detect(file, "Reformated|Playing around|Sandy Beach Only|^Copy of OPIHI 2024") ~ "D: derived/compiled",
      str_detect(file, "^OPIHI data (19|20)\\d{2}")                                     ~ "A: legacy blocks",
      str_detect(file, "Field Study")                                                    ~ "C: classroom group totals",
      str_detect(file, "2024 datasheet|BIOL 499|Longitudinal|RAW Mauliola")              ~ "B: modern row-per-quadrat",
      TRUE ~ "UNCLASSIFIED - check"
    ),
    n_tabs = map_int(file.path(RAW_DIR, file), \(f) length(readxl::excel_sheets(f)))
  ) |>
  arrange(family, file)

knitr::kable(inventory, caption = "Raw Excel files and the format family each belongs to.")
```

### Convert raw Excel to open CSV

Every tab of every raw workbook is written unchanged to
`Data/Processed/raw_csv/`, so the raw data are preserved in a
non-proprietary format. Tabs that contain no cells (Excel chart sheets,
which only hold a graph) cannot be exported and are listed below rather
than skipped silently.

```{r export-csv}
csv_log <- export_raw_csv(RAW_DIR, CSV_DIR)
cat(sum(csv_log$status == "exported"), "of", nrow(csv_log), "tabs from",
    n_distinct(csv_log$file), "workbooks written to Data/Processed/raw_csv\n")

csv_log |>
  filter(status != "exported") |>
  select(file, sheet, status) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Tabs not exported to CSV (chart sheets with no cell data).")
```

## 2. Cleaning decisions log

Decisions agreed by the team, applied by code (never by hand-editing raw
files).

| \# | Issue | Decision |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | Rows labelled "EXAMPLE" (student templates) | Remove; log in exclusions |
| 2 | Metadata date differs from data-row date (e.g. Mauliola 2026: 4/26 vs 4/20) | Data-row date wins; metadata date likely the sheet creation date |
| 3 | Times like 01:14 for a field trip | Times standardised to 24-h HH:MM. Hours 01–05 assumed PM (+12 h) and flagged |
| 4 | `#REF!` and other spreadsheet errors | Set to NA |
| 5 | Site spellings | One canonical spelling per site: **Hawaiian name first**, no ʻokina or kahakō; English name kept as alias. Misspellings flagged with a suggested match |
| 6 | Taxon names | All taxa harmonised via a crosswalk table (raw name → clean name) |
| 7 | Classroom group-total files | Kept with `resolution = "group_total"`; excluded from detection frequency |
| 8 | Transect point-intercept data | Not in the master (quadrat data only); possible secondary table |
| 9 | Blank cells | Blank cell in a filled quadrat = 0 (not detected); entirely blank row = missing |
| 10 | Legacy block with no date/site/school (2020 file, block 8) | Excluded; logged |
| 11 | Legacy quadrat column with data but blank header | Kept; transect/quadrat inferred from neighbours; flagged `inferred` |
| 12 | Teacher IDs | Legacy: School is the teacher stand-in. Modern: Team Leader. One anonymised ID per survey (site + date); several leaders → IDs sorted and joined with `;`. Names split on `,` / `and` / `&`, trimmed, case-fixed first |
| 13 | Student names ("Data Entry By") | Not in the public master (not needed for Question C; protects students) |
| 14 | Modern rows with no date and all taxa blank/0 | Leftover template rows; excluded as `blank_template_row` |
| 15 | Modern rows with date/site but no taxon entries | Quadrat not entered; excluded as `no_taxon_data`, not counted as effort |
| 16 | Unreadable date cell (e.g. a name typed in Date) | If the rows before and after share date and site, use it and flag `date_inferred`; otherwise NA, flag `invalid_date` |
| 17 | Sheet `Total Points` ≠ sum of the row's cells | Keep the cell counts (the typed total is the error); flag `total_points_mismatch` |
| 18 | `Column Totals` summary rows | Excluded as `summary_row` |
| 19 | Derived tabs (PercentCover, Grouped sums) | Not imported; calculated from PtCounts, so they would duplicate data |

## 3. Import Family A: legacy files (2004–2020)

Family A is exactly these 9 workbooks (one tab each). Note the 2020
file's tab is named `All_raw_data_OPIHI_16-20`, but it only contains
2020 field trips.

| File | Tab | Field-trip blocks |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `OPIHI data 2004.xlsx` | OPIHI data 2004 | 3 |
| `OPIHI data 2005.xlsx` | OPIHI data 2005 | 16 |
| `OPIHI data 2006 and 2007.xlsx` | OPIHI data 2006 and 2007 | 24 |
| `OPIHI data 2008 might be mis-type....xlsx` | OPIHI data 2008 (might be mis-t | 1 |
| `OPIHI data 2016.xlsx` | OPIHI data 2016 | 33 |
| `OPIHI data 2017.xlsx` | OPIHI data 2017 | 56 |
| `OPIHI data 2018.xlsx` | OPIHI data 2018 | 33 |
| `OPIHI data 2019.xlsx` | OPIHI data 2019 | 54 |
| `OPIHI data 2020.xlsx` | All_raw_data_OPIHI_16-20 | 8 (1 has no metadata) |

```{r import-legacy}
# Each Family A file is identified by how its name STARTS, so small changes to
# the rest of the name (e.g. "..." becoming "…" after a download) don't break it.
LEGACY_KEYS <- c("2004", "2005", "2006 and 2007", "2008", "2016",
                 "2017", "2018", "2019", "2020")
raw_files <- list_raw_xlsx(RAW_DIR, full.names = FALSE)
legacy_match <- tibble(key = LEGACY_KEYS) |>
  mutate(files   = purrr::map(key, \(k) raw_files[str_starts(raw_files, fixed(paste("OPIHI data", k)))]),
         n_found = lengths(files))
if (any(legacy_match$n_found != 1)) {
  print(legacy_match)
  stop("Each Family A year should match exactly one file in ", RAW_DIR,
       ". Check the rows above where n_found is not 1.")
}
LEGACY_FILES <- unlist(legacy_match$files)

legacy <- import_legacy(RAW_DIR)
stopifnot(setequal(unique(legacy$surveys$source_file), LEGACY_FILES))  # importer read exactly these 9

tibble(
  item = c("legacy files", "field-trip blocks", "quadrats",
           "non-empty count cells", "distinct raw taxon names"),
  n = c(n_distinct(legacy$surveys$source_file), nrow(legacy$surveys),
        nrow(legacy$quadrats), nrow(legacy$counts), n_distinct(legacy$counts$taxon_raw))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Family A import summary.")
```

### Verification against the spreadsheets' own totals

Each legacy block has a `TOTALS:` section computed in Excel. If our
parser read the sideways blocks correctly, re-summing our long-format
counts must reproduce every one of those totals.

```{r verify-legacy}
mismatch <- check_legacy_totals(legacy)
cat("Sheet TOTALS rows checked:", sum(!is.na(legacy$totals$sheet_total)),
    "| mismatches:", nrow(mismatch), "\n")
if (nrow(mismatch) > 0) knitr::kable(mismatch)
```

```{r legacy-issues}
legacy$issues |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Issues flagged while parsing legacy files (nothing dropped silently).")
```

```{r legacy-point-sums}
# Each quadrat has 25 points. Sums < 25 are expected (bare substrate was often
# not recorded); sums > 25 are flagged for review, not removed.
quad_sums <- legacy$counts |>
  group_by(block_id, transect, quadrat) |>
  summarise(points = sum(count), .groups = "drop")
cat("Quadrats with point sum > 25:", sum(quad_sums$points > 25), "of", nrow(quad_sums), "\n")
```

## 4. Import Family B: modern row-per-quadrat files

Family B is these 4 workbooks. Only the `Quadrat PtCounts` tab is
imported, plus `Metadata`. The other tabs (PercentCover, Grouped sums)
are calculated from PtCounts, so importing them would duplicate data.
`Copy of OPIHI 2024 datasheet` is a 6-row subset of the 2024 file
(Family D) and is not imported.

| File | Quadrats kept | Rows excluded |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| `OPIHI 2024 datasheet .xlsx` | 624 | 294 blank template rows |
| `OPIHI BIOL 499 2025 LT data.xlsx` | 81 | 1 no taxon data |
| `OPIHI 2026 Longitudinal Monitoring Data.xlsx` | 75 | 107 no taxon data, 15 blank template, 1 EXAMPLE |
| `RAW Mauliola OPIHI Data 2026.xlsx` | 54 | 1 no taxon data, 1 Column Totals row |

```{r import-modern}
MODERN_KEYS <- c("OPIHI 2024 datasheet", "OPIHI BIOL 499 2025",
                 "OPIHI 2026 Longitudinal", "RAW Mauliola")
modern_match <- tibble(key = MODERN_KEYS) |>
  mutate(files = purrr::map(key, \(k) raw_files[str_starts(raw_files, fixed(k))]),
         n_found = lengths(files))
if (any(modern_match$n_found != 1)) {
  print(modern_match)
  stop("Each Family B key should match exactly one file in ", RAW_DIR, ".")
}
MODERN_FILES <- unlist(modern_match$files)

modern <- import_modern(MODERN_FILES, RAW_DIR)

tibble(
  item = c("modern files", "quadrats kept", "non-empty count cells",
           "distinct raw taxon names", "rows excluded", "metadata rows"),
  n = c(n_distinct(modern$quadrats$source_file), nrow(modern$quadrats),
        nrow(modern$counts), n_distinct(modern$counts$taxon_raw),
        nrow(modern$excluded), nrow(modern$metadata))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Family B import summary.")
```

```{r modern-excluded}
modern$excluded |>
  count(source_file, reason, name = "rows") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Family B rows excluded, by rule.")
```

### Verification against the sheets' own row totals

Each modern row has a `Total Points` column typed or calculated on the
sheet. Re-summing our parsed counts should match it, except where the
sheet's total itself is wrong (flagged, and our sum from the cells is
used).

```{r verify-modern}
checked <- sum(!is.na(modern$quadrats$total_points_sheet))
n_mism  <- sum(modern$issues$issue == "total_points_mismatch")
cat("Rows with a sheet Total Points:", checked, "| match:", checked - n_mism,
    "| mismatch:", n_mism, "\n")

modern$issues |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Issues flagged on kept Family B rows.")
```

```{r modern-categories}
modern$counts |>
  count(sheet_category, name = "count_cells") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Count cells by the category label printed on the datasheet.")
```

## 5. Import Family C: classroom group totals

These 3 workbooks record **student-group totals** (each group's points
summed over its quadrats), so they cannot give per-quadrat detection.
They are kept with `resolution = "group_total"`, and each group's effort
comes from its `TOTAL Points` row (points / 25 = quadrats). 2023 and
2025 name no site or date anywhere in the file, so only the year (from
the file name) is known.

| File | Groups | Quadrats per group | Site / date |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| `Copy of OPIHI Field Study 2023 - ALL Group Data P1_P2.xlsx` | 14 | 7 | none in file |
| `Copy of OPIHI Field Study 2025 - ALL Group Data P1_P2 - use this one.xlsx` | 14 | 6 | none in file |
| `OPIHI Field Study 2026 - Waipuilani Data.xlsx` | 6 | 11 | Waipuilani, 2026-04-20 and 2026-05-04 |

```{r import-classroom}
CLASS_KEYS <- c("Copy of OPIHI Field Study 2023", "Copy of OPIHI Field Study 2025",
                "OPIHI Field Study 2026")
class_match <- tibble(key = CLASS_KEYS) |>
  mutate(files = purrr::map(key, \(k) raw_files[str_starts(raw_files, fixed(k))]),
         n_found = lengths(files))
if (any(class_match$n_found != 1)) {
  print(class_match)
  stop("Each Family C key should match exactly one file in ", RAW_DIR, ".")
}
CLASS_FILES <- unlist(class_match$files)

classroom <- import_classroom(CLASS_FILES, RAW_DIR, known_sites = unique(site_xw$site_name))

classroom$groups |>
  count(source_file, date, n_quadrats, name = "groups") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Family C student groups per file and date.")

classroom$issues |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Issues flagged in Family C.")
```

## 6. Site and taxon harmonisation

Names are standardised with two **editable lookup tables** in
`Data/Lookups/`. Each raw spelling is reduced to a *key* (lower case,
extra spaces removed; for sites also ʻokina, apostrophes and kahakō
removed), and the key is looked up in the table. To fix or add a name,
edit the CSV, not the code.

- `site_crosswalk.csv`: raw site key → `site_name` (Hawaiian name first,
  no ʻokina/kahakō), `site_alias_english`, `island`.
- `taxon_crosswalk.csv`: raw taxon key → `taxon_clean` (spelling fixed,
  current name), `analysis_taxon` (usually genus, matching OPIHI's ID
  resolution), `category` (Algae, Cyanobacteria, Invertebrate, Coral,
  Substrate, Unknown, Invalid). Lines marked `REVIEW` are judgement
  calls worth checking.

Any name **not** in a lookup is listed with the closest existing key as
a suggestion (edit distance); it is never matched automatically.

```{r lookups}
cat("Site lookup:", nrow(site_xw), "spellings ->", n_distinct(site_xw$site_name), "sites\n")
cat("Taxon lookup:", nrow(taxon_xw), "spellings ->", n_distinct(taxon_xw$taxon_clean), "clean taxa ->",
    n_distinct(taxon_xw$analysis_taxon[taxon_xw$analysis_taxon != ""]), "analysis taxa\n")
```

### Reusable function: checking taxon names in new data

`standardize_taxa()` (in `Scripts/clean_build.R`) checks taxon names
against the team's lookup table, `Data/Lookups/taxon_crosswalk.csv`.
**Input:** a vector of taxon names as written on a datasheet, plus the
lookup table. **Output:** one row per distinct name, giving its
standardised name (`taxon_clean`), its coarser `analysis_taxon`, and its
`category`. A name that is not in the lookup gets `NA` and a
`taxon_suggestion`: the closest known name by spelling. A name that is
just a number is marked `Invalid`. OPIHI can run it on any new datasheet
before adding it to the master: known misspellings are fixed
automatically, and new typos or new species are listed for a person to
check, never matched silently. Fixing one means adding a line to the
lookup CSV, not changing code. `standardize_sites()` works the same way
for site names. The test below uses four names: a correct one, a known
misspelling, a new typo, and a number typed into the name column.

```{r test-standardize-taxa}
test_names <- c("Acanthophora spicifera",  # correct name
                "Turbinania ornata",       # known misspelling, already in the lookup
                "Acanthophora spicifra",   # new typo, not in the lookup
                "3.0")                     # number typed where a name belongs
test_out <- standardize_taxa(test_names, taxon_xw)
knitr::kable(select(test_out, taxon_raw, taxon_clean, category, taxon_suggestion),
             caption = "Test of standardize_taxa() on four example names.")

stopifnot(
  test_out$taxon_clean[1] == "Acanthophora spicifera",      # correct name kept
  test_out$taxon_clean[2] == "Turbinaria ornata",           # misspelling fixed
  is.na(test_out$taxon_clean[3]),                           # new typo flagged...
  test_out$taxon_suggestion[3] == "acanthophora spicifera", # ...with the right suggestion
  test_out$category[4] == "Invalid"                         # number rejected
)
cat("All standardize_taxa() tests passed.\n")
```

## 7. Build: harmonise, deduplicate, cross-check

`build_opihi()` (in `Scripts/clean_build.R`) combines the three imports
and applies:

- **Sites** via the crosswalk, then a **coordinate check** (legacy trips
  have coordinates): if a trip's coordinates are \> 5 km from its
  labelled site but match another site's coordinates (\< 0.2 km), it is
  relabelled and flagged `site_corrected_by_coordinates`; \> 5 km with
  no match is flagged only.
- **Taxa** via the crosswalk; `Invalid` entries (e.g. a number typed as
  a taxon) excluded and logged.
- **Times**: 24-h HH:MM; legacy placeholder times (00:00–01:00) removed;
  hours 01–05 assumed PM; all flagged.
- **Teacher IDs**: legacy School / modern Team Leader → anonymous `T###`
  per person or school, in order of first appearance; several per survey
  → `T001;T004`. The name → ID key is written **only** to
  `Data/Processed/private/`.
- **Duplicates**: (a) identical survey content in two places (kept
  once),
  (b) identical quadrats within a survey, (c) same site + date in two
      different files with different content (flagged, not removed).
- **Cross-check** of every trip in the compiled files (Family D) against
  the master.

```{r build}
compiled <- bind_rows(
  read_compiled_trips(file.path(RAW_DIR, raw_files[str_starts(raw_files, "OPIHI Data - Reformated")])),
  read_compiled_trips(file.path(RAW_DIR, raw_files[str_starts(raw_files, "Sandy Beach Only")]))
)

opihi <- build_opihi(legacy, modern, classroom, site_xw, taxon_xw, compiled)

tibble(
  table = c("surveys", "samples (quadrats + student groups)", "master rows (detections)",
            "clean taxa in master", "analysis taxa in master", "teacher IDs", "excluded records", "QC flags"),
  n = c(nrow(opihi$surveys), nrow(opihi$samples), nrow(opihi$master),
        n_distinct(opihi$master$taxon_clean), n_distinct(opihi$master$analysis_taxon),
        nrow(opihi$teacher_key), nrow(opihi$exclusions), nrow(opihi$qc_flags))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Final processed data summary.")
```

```{r unmatched}
if (nrow(opihi$unmatched) == 0) {
  cat("All site and taxon names matched a lookup entry.\n")
} else {
  knitr::kable(opihi$unmatched, caption = "Names missing from the lookups (add them to the CSVs).")
}
```

```{r exclusions-summary}
opihi$exclusions |>
  count(level, reason, name = "records") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Records excluded from the master, by rule (full list in opihi_exclusions_log.csv).")
```

```{r qc-summary}
opihi$qc_flags |>
  separate_rows(flag, sep = ";") |>
  count(level, flag, name = "records") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "QC flags kept in the data (full list in opihi_qc_flags.csv).")
```

```{r crosscheck}
opihi$crosscheck |>
  count(source_file, status, name = "trips") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Every trip listed in the compiled files, checked against the master.")
```

## 8. Write the processed data

```{r write-outputs}
PRIVATE_DIR <- file.path(CLEAN_DIR, "private")
dir.create(PRIVATE_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)

write_csv(opihi$master,     file.path(CLEAN_DIR, "opihi_master.csv"),            na = "")
write_csv(opihi$surveys,    file.path(CLEAN_DIR, "opihi_surveys.csv"),           na = "")
write_csv(opihi$samples,    file.path(CLEAN_DIR, "opihi_samples.csv"),           na = "")
write_csv(opihi$exclusions, file.path(CLEAN_DIR, "opihi_exclusions_log.csv"),    na = "")
write_csv(opihi$qc_flags,   file.path(CLEAN_DIR, "opihi_qc_flags.csv"),          na = "")
write_csv(opihi$crosscheck, file.path(CLEAN_DIR, "opihi_compiled_crosscheck.csv"), na = "")
write_csv(opihi$unmatched,  file.path(CLEAN_DIR, "opihi_unmatched_names.csv"),   na = "")
# PRIVATE: real names -> anonymous IDs. For Joanna only; never commit or share.
write_csv(opihi$teacher_key, file.path(PRIVATE_DIR, "teacher_key_PRIVATE.csv"),  na = "")

list.files(CLEAN_DIR, pattern = "\\.csv$")
```

### Data dictionary

```{r data-dictionary}
data_dictionary <- tribble(
  ~table, ~column, ~type, ~description,
  "master", "survey_id", "text", "Survey (site visit) ID, S0001..., ordered by date; joins to opihi_surveys",
  "master", "sample_id", "text", "Sample ID (one quadrat, or one student group); joins to opihi_samples",
  "master", "date", "date", "Survey date (YYYY-MM-DD); blank if the source file records none",
  "master", "year", "integer", "Survey year (from the date, or from the file name for undated classroom files)",
  "master", "site_name", "text", "Standardised site name, Hawaiian name first, no ʻokina/kahakō",
  "master", "site_alias_english", "text", "English name of the site where one is in common use",
  "master", "island", "text", "Island",
  "master", "latitude / longitude", "number", "Decimal degrees as recorded on legacy datasheets (blank for modern files)",
  "master", "teacher_id", "text", "Anonymous teacher/school/team-leader ID(s); several joined with ';'",
  "master", "resolution", "text", "'quadrat' = one row per quadrat; 'group_total' = classroom group totals",
  "master", "sample_type", "text", "'quadrat' or 'student_group'",
  "master", "group_label", "text", "Student-group label (classroom files only), e.g. P1G3",
  "master", "transect", "integer", "Transect number within the survey",
  "master", "quadrat", "integer", "Quadrat number along the transect (legacy files only)",
  "master", "point_m", "number", "Quadrat position along the transect in metres",
  "master", "n_quadrats", "number", "Quadrats in the sample: 1 for quadrats; group size for student groups",
  "master", "taxon_raw", "text", "Taxon or substrate name exactly as written on the datasheet",
  "master", "taxon_clean", "text", "Standardised name: spelling fixed, current taxonomy (see taxon_crosswalk.csv)",
  "master", "analysis_taxon", "text", "Coarser name for consistent comparison across years (usually genus)",
  "master", "category", "text", "Algae, Cyanobacteria, Invertebrate, Coral, Substrate or Unknown",
  "master", "count", "number", "Point-intercept hits for this taxon in the sample (> 0; absences are implied)",
  "master", "points_possible", "number", "25 x n_quadrats",
  "master", "sample_flag", "text", "QC flags on the sample, ';'-separated (see opihi_qc_flags.csv)",
  "master", "source_family", "text", "Raw-file format family: A legacy, B modern, C classroom",
  "master", "source_cell", "text", "Raw file and Excel row/column the value came from",
  "surveys", "start_time / stop_time / low_tide_time", "text", "24-hour HH:MM; placeholders removed, 01-05 h assumed PM (flagged)",
  "surveys", "n_transects_reported / n_quad_per_t_reported", "integer", "Effort written on the legacy datasheet (may differ from actual)",
  "surveys", "n_samples / n_quadrats", "integer", "Actual samples and quadrats in the cleaned data (sampling effort)",
  "surveys", "src_key", "text", "Internal key back to the raw file/block",
  "samples", "point_sum", "number", "Sum of all counts in the sample (25 expected per quadrat in modern files)",
  "samples", "n_taxa", "integer", "Distinct non-substrate taxa recorded in the sample",
  "samples", "sample_key", "text", "Internal key back to the raw file/row/column"
)
write_csv(data_dictionary, file.path(CLEAN_DIR, "opihi_data_dictionary.csv"))
knitr::kable(data_dictionary, caption = "Data dictionary (also written to opihi_data_dictionary.csv).")
```

### Preview of the master data

```{r master-preview}
opihi$master |>
  filter(analysis_taxon %in% c("Acanthophora spicifera", "Avrainvillea spp.", "Gracilaria spp.",
                               "Turbinaria ornata", "Cellana spp.")) |>
  select(survey_id, date, site_name, island, taxon_clean, count, points_possible) |>
  slice_head(n = 12) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "First rows of the master for some taxa of interest.")
```

# 2nd Script: Data Cleaning Verification and Corrections

## About this script

This script independently checks the AI-built OPIHI master dataset
against the raw Excel datasheets, applies the corrections that came out
of those checks, and writes the final files.

- **Inputs:** the raw workbooks in `AI_data/Data/Raw/` (kept locally
  only, not on GitHub) and the AI pipeline's outputs in
  `AI_data/Data/Processed/`.
- **Outputs:** `opihi_master_completed.csv`,
  `opihi_surveys_completed.csv`, `opihi_samples_completed.csv` and
  `opihi_change_log.csv`, written to `AI_data/Data/Processed/`. The
  pipeline's original files are not changed.
- **How to run:** open the project (`GroupC_AI_Data_Sprint.Rproj`), then
  run all chunks top to bottom or press **Render**.
- **Expected values** are written as comments next to each check (for
  example `# expect 0`).
- **Manual checks** (opening the raw Excel files by hand) are described
  in the text where they informed a decision.

The record of how this was developed with AI (prompts, answers, mistakes
and decisions) is kept separately in
`AI_data/OPIHI_Data_Cleaning_Verification_Crosschecking_Summary.pdf`.

## Setup

Load the AI pipeline's processed files.

```{r}
#| label: setup-verification

proc_dir <- here("Data", "Processed")
raw_dir <- here("Data", "Raw")

opihi_master              <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_master.csv"))
opihi_samples             <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_samples.csv"))
opihi_surveys             <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_surveys.csv"))
opihi_qc_flags            <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_qc_flags.csv"))
opihi_exclusions_log      <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_exclusions_log.csv"))
opihi_unmatched_names     <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_unmatched_names.csv"))
opihi_data_dictionary     <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_data_dictionary.csv"))
opihi_compiled_crosscheck <- read_csv(file.path(proc_dir, "opihi_compiled_crosscheck.csv"))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Part 1 · Does every master value come from a raw cell?

Tests whether the AI copied every count correctly from the raw
workbooks, without changing or inventing values. The master's
`source_cell` column records the raw file, tab, row and column of each
value, so every row can be looked up in the raw file.

### 1.1 Read the source location of each master row

Splits `source_cell` into file, tab, row and column. The file name is
read up to `.xlsx` (one file name contains a `!`, which is also the
separator before the row), and the row is taken from the last `!R`.

```{r}
#| label: parse-source-cell
master_src <- opihi_master |>
  mutate(
    master_id = row_number(),                                         # one ID per master row
    src_file  = str_extract(source_cell, "(?i)^.*?\\.xls[xm]?"),
    src_sheet = str_match(source_cell, "\\|(.+)!R\\d+")[, 2],          # tab (Family C only)
    src_row   = as.integer(str_match(source_cell, ".*!R(\\d+)")[, 2]),
    src_col   = as.integer(str_match(source_cell, "C(\\d+)$")[, 2])
  )

# every row should have a file and a row number: expect 0 rows
master_src |> filter(is.na(src_file) | is.na(src_row)) |> count(source_family)
```

### 1.2 Read every raw cell with its true position

Reads every non-blank cell of every raw workbook. `tidyxl` keeps the
real Excel row and column numbers; `readxl` can skip leading blank rows
and shift them.

```{r}
#| label: raw-cells
raw_files <- list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
raw_files <- raw_files[!str_detect(basename(raw_files), "^~\\$")]   # skip Excel lock files

raw_cells <- purrr::map(raw_files, \(p) {
  xlsx_cells(p) |>
    filter(!is_blank) |>
    transmute(src_file = basename(p), sheet, row, col, data_type, numeric, character)
}) |> list_rbind()

# master files that don't exist in Raw: expect character(0)
setdiff(unique(master_src$src_file), unique(raw_cells$src_file))
```

### 1.3 Families A and B (legacy and modern sheets)

Families A and B don't record the tab in `source_cell`, and the same row
and column can exist on several tabs of one workbook. A value therefore
only counts as a match when the cell holds the same number **and** the
taxon name sits in the same row or column on that tab. Each master row
keeps its best result.

```{r}
#| label: ab-check
# every text cell, as a lower-case label, by row and by column
labels <- raw_cells |>
  filter(data_type == "character") |>
  transmute(src_file, sheet, row, col, label = str_squish(str_to_lower(character)))

row_labels <- labels |> distinct(src_file, sheet, row, label) |> mutate(label_in_row = TRUE)
col_labels <- labels |> distinct(src_file, sheet, col, label) |> mutate(label_in_col = TRUE)

ab2 <- master_src |>
  filter(source_family %in% c("A", "B")) |>
  mutate(taxon_key = str_squish(str_to_lower(taxon_raw))) |>
  left_join(raw_cells,
            by = c("src_file", "src_row" = "row", "src_col" = "col"),
            relationship = "many-to-many") |>                         # one hit per tab
  left_join(row_labels, by = c("src_file", "sheet", "src_row" = "row", "taxon_key" = "label")) |>
  left_join(col_labels, by = c("src_file", "sheet", "src_col" = "col", "taxon_key" = "label")) |>
  mutate(
    label_ok = coalesce(label_in_row, FALSE) | coalesce(label_in_col, FALSE),
    value_ok = !is.na(numeric) & numeric == count,
    status = case_when(
      label_ok & value_ok                 ~ "1 match",
      label_ok & data_type %in% "numeric" ~ "2 value mismatch",
      label_ok                            ~ "3 raw cell not numeric",
      value_ok                            ~ "4 value matches, taxon label not found on that tab",
      TRUE                                ~ "5 no usable match"
    ))

# keep the best result for each master row
ab_best2 <- ab2 |> arrange(master_id, status) |> distinct(master_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

nrow(ab_best2)                            # expect 22,241 (all A + B rows)
ab_best2 |> count(source_family, status)  # expect only "1 match"
```

**Result:** all 22,241 Family A and B rows match a raw cell on a
specific tab, with the right taxon label.

### 1.4 Family C (classroom group files), forward check

Family C records the tab and row; the column comes from the sample's
`sample_key` in `opihi_samples`. Same matching rule as above (value plus
taxon label in the same row).

```{r}
#| label: c-forward
c_check <- master_src |>
  filter(source_family == "C") |>
  left_join(opihi_samples |> select(sample_id, sample_key), by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(
    src_col   = as.integer(str_match(sample_key, "\\|c(\\d+)$")[, 2]),   # group column
    taxon_key = str_squish(str_to_lower(taxon_raw))
  ) |>
  left_join(raw_cells, by = c("src_file", "src_sheet" = "sheet", "src_row" = "row", "src_col" = "col")) |>
  left_join(row_labels, by = c("src_file", "src_sheet" = "sheet", "src_row" = "row", "taxon_key" = "label")) |>
  mutate(
    label_ok = coalesce(label_in_row, FALSE),
    value_ok = !is.na(numeric) & numeric == count,
    status = case_when(
      label_ok & value_ok                 ~ "match",
      label_ok & data_type %in% "numeric" ~ "value mismatch",
      label_ok                            ~ "raw cell not numeric",
      value_ok                            ~ "value matches, taxon label not in that row",
      TRUE                                ~ "no usable match"
    ))

nrow(c_check)          # expect 347
c_check |> count(status)
```

**Result:** 347 of 347 match. Families A, B and C together (22,241 + 347
= 22,588) cover the whole master.

### 1.5 Family C, reverse check: is any raw count missing from master?

Collects every non-zero count in the raw group columns and checks that
each one appears in master. Data rows lie between the "Organism" and
"TOTAL" labels; these sit in column A on most tabs and in column B on
the 2025 P1 tab and the Waipuilani file, so both columns are searched.

```{r}
#| label: c-reverse
# the group columns of each tab, from the sample keys
c_cols <- opihi_samples |>
  filter(survey_id %in% master_src$survey_id[master_src$source_family == "C"]) |>
  transmute(src_file  = str_extract(sample_key, "^[^|]+"),
            src_sheet = str_match(sample_key, "^[^|]+\\|([^|]+)\\|")[, 2],
            src_col   = as.integer(str_match(sample_key, "\\|c(\\d+)$")[, 2])) |>
  distinct()
anyNA(c_cols)    # expect FALSE

# first and last data row of each tab
c_layout <- raw_cells |>
  semi_join(c_cols, by = c("src_file", "sheet" = "src_sheet")) |>
  filter(col %in% 1:2, data_type == "character") |>
  group_by(src_file, sheet) |>
  summarise(first_row = min(row[str_detect(character, regex("^organism", ignore_case = TRUE))]),
            last_row  = min(row[str_detect(character, regex("^total", ignore_case = TRUE))]),
            .groups = "drop")
c_layout    # expect no Inf

# every non-zero raw count in those rows and columns
raw_c <- raw_cells |>
  inner_join(c_cols,   by = c("src_file", "sheet" = "src_sheet", "col" = "src_col")) |>
  inner_join(c_layout, by = c("src_file", "sheet")) |>
  filter(row > first_row, row < last_row, data_type == "numeric", numeric > 0)

in_master <- c_check |> distinct(src_file, src_sheet, src_row, src_col)

nrow(raw_c)    # expect 347
raw_c |> anti_join(in_master,
  by = c("src_file", "sheet" = "src_sheet", "row" = "src_row", "col" = "src_col")) |>
  select(src_file, sheet, row, col, numeric)    # raw counts missing from master: expect 0 rows

# numbers stored as text would escape the check above: expect 0
raw_cells |>
  inner_join(c_cols, by = c("src_file", "sheet" = "src_sheet", "col" = "src_col")) |>
  filter(data_type == "character", str_detect(character, "^\\s*[0-9.]+\\s*$")) |> nrow()
```

**Result:** 347 raw counts, all in master, and no numbers stored as
text. Family C is verified in both directions.

*Note:* the team later replaced the Waipuilani workbook in `Raw/` with a
re-saved copy. A cell-by-cell comparison with the copy first checked
found only cosmetic differences (line-break characters and recalculated
proportion formulas), so this result holds for the current file.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Part 2 · Does the master agree with the sample table?

Recomputes each sample's point total and number of taxa from master and
compares them with `opihi_samples`.

```{r}
#| label: master-vs-samples
master_totals <- opihi_master |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  summarise(master_sum = sum(count), master_taxa = n(), .groups = "drop")

sample_mismatch <- opihi_samples |>
  left_join(master_totals, by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(master_sum = replace_na(master_sum, 0), master_taxa = replace_na(master_taxa, 0)) |>
  filter(point_sum != master_sum | n_taxa != master_taxa)

nrow(sample_mismatch)                                         # 730: all differ in n_taxa only
sample_mismatch |> count(sum_off = point_sum != master_sum)   # expect FALSE only: sums always agree
```

The 730 differences are all in the taxon count and all in the modern
files. The data dictionary defines `n_taxa` as **non-substrate** taxa,
while the count above includes Rock, sand and Rubble rows, which only
modern sheets record. Recounting without substrate:

```{r}
#| label: n-taxa-definition
opihi_master |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  summarise(ns_clean    = n_distinct(taxon_clean[!category %in% "Substrate"]),
            ns_analysis = n_distinct(analysis_taxon[!category %in% "Substrate"]),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(opihi_samples |> select(sample_id, n_taxa), by = "sample_id") |>
  summarise(clean_disagree = sum(ns_clean != n_taxa),          # expect 0
            analysis_disagree = sum(ns_analysis != n_taxa))     # > 0 is expected (genus level)
```

**Result:** point totals agree in all 7,216 samples, and taxon counts
agree once substrate is excluded.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Part 3 · Duplicate visits and surveys without a site

Looks for the same site and date entered as more than one survey, and
for raw files that contribute nothing to master.

```{r}
#| label: same-site-same-date
# any site and date that appears in more than one survey
opihi_surveys |>
  group_by(site_name, date) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  arrange(site_name, date) |>
  select(survey_id, source_file, site_name, date, resolution, n_samples) |>
  print(n = Inf)

# raw files that contribute nothing to master (expected: the Family D cross-check files)
setdiff(basename(raw_files), unique(master_src$src_file))
```

**Result:** no visit is entered twice. The same-site, same-day pairs
come from one file each with very different totals, so they are separate
groups. Two classroom surveys have no site or date: **S0251** (2023
group file) and **S0252** (2025 group file). `opihi_unmatched_names`
cannot detect this, because a missing site never appears as an unmatched
name.

### 3.1 Recover S0251's site and transects

*Manual check:* every chart in the 2023 group file is titled "Diamond
Head (Le'ahi)", although no cell holds the site. The group labels (P1G1
… P2G7) give the transect number after the G.

This chunk fills S0251's site from the existing Leahi surveys and its
transects from the group labels, adds flag columns (`site_recovered`,
`transect_inferred`), and starts the change log. All later corrections
are applied to the `_completed` copies, never to the original tables.

```{r}
#| label: recover-s0251
# Leahi's details, taken from the existing legacy surveys
site_info <- opihi_surveys |>
  filter(site_name == "Leahi") |>
  group_by(site_name, site_alias_english, island) |>
  summarise(latitude = median(latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
            longitude = median(longitude, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
nrow(site_info)   # expect 1

# set S0251's site columns to Leahi and flag them
fill_s0251 <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      site_recovered     = survey_id == "S0251",
      site_name          = if_else(site_recovered, site_info$site_name, site_name),
      site_alias_english = if_else(site_recovered, site_info$site_alias_english, site_alias_english),
      island             = if_else(site_recovered, site_info$island, island)
    )
}

# take S0251's transect from the group label (P1G3 -> transect 3) and flag it
fill_transect <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      transect_inferred = survey_id == "S0251",
      transect = if_else(transect_inferred,
                         as.numeric(str_extract(group_label, "(?<=G)\\d+")),
                         transect)
    )
}

surveys_completed <- opihi_surveys |>
  fill_s0251() |>
  mutate(recovery_source = if_else(site_recovered,
         "chart title 'Diamond Head (Le'ahi)' on all tabs of the 2023 group file; not in any cell",
         NA_character_))

master_completed  <- opihi_master  |> fill_s0251() |> fill_transect()
samples_completed <- opihi_samples |> fill_transect()   # keeps samples consistent with master

# checks: only S0251's site and transect columns changed
anti_join(opihi_master, master_completed,
          by = setdiff(names(opihi_master), c("site_name", "site_alias_english", "island", "transect"))) |>
  nrow()                                                       # expect 0
master_completed |> count(site_recovered)                      # TRUE = 125
master_completed |> filter(is.na(site_name)) |> count(survey_id)   # only S0252
sum(master_completed$count) == sum(opihi_master$count)         # TRUE

# start the change log (one row per correction)
change_log <- tibble(
  change = c("S0251: site recovered as Leahi (site_name, site_alias_english, island)",
             "S0251: transect filled from the group label (P#G# -> transect #)"),
  rows   = c(sum(master_completed$site_recovered), sum(master_completed$transect_inferred)),
  reason = c("chart titles in the 2023 group file name Diamond Head (Le'ahi); no cell holds the site",
             "group labels encode the transect; column left blank by the cleaning"))
```

S0252 (2025 group file) stays without a site: nothing in that file
identifies one.

**Splitting S0251 and S0252 by tab (P1/P2):** not done. A survey should
be one site visit, but S0251's charts name Diamond Head on both tabs and
neither tab has a date, so there is no evidence that P1 and P2 were
different visits (P most likely means class period). S0252 has no site
or date on either tab, so there is nothing to split on. Both stay as one
survey each; their dates remain unknown (year only).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Part 4 · QC flags

Checks that every flag in `opihi_qc_flags` points to a real record and
that each flagging rule was applied correctly.

```{r}
#| label: qc-overview
opihi_qc_flags |> count(level, flag, sort = TRUE) |> print(n = Inf)

# do flagged samples exist? expect 0
opihi_qc_flags |> filter(level == "sample") |>
  anti_join(opihi_samples, by = c("ref" = "sample_id")) |> nrow()
```

**Result:** 296 flags; every sample-level flag points to a real sample.
Four cells hold two flags joined by `;`, so the tests below search
inside the text.

### 4.1 Is `points_over_25` applied correctly?

Rebuilds the list of samples whose points exceed the possible total and
compares it with the flagged list in both directions.

```{r}
#| label: points-over-25
over_flagged <- opihi_qc_flags |>
  filter(level == "sample", str_detect(flag, "points_over_25")) |>
  distinct(ref)
over_data <- opihi_samples |> filter(point_sum > points_possible)

nrow(over_flagged); nrow(over_data)    # both 230
over_data |> anti_join(over_flagged, by = c("sample_id" = "ref")) |> nrow()   # missed flags: 0
over_flagged |> anti_join(over_data, by = c("ref" = "sample_id")) |> nrow()   # wrong flags: 0

# split by family, to compare with the handoff guide's 174 for legacy files
over_data |>
  left_join(opihi_master |> distinct(sample_id, source_family), by = "sample_id") |>
  count(source_family, sample_type)
```

**Result:** the rule is exactly right: 230 over the limit, all flagged,
none flagged wrongly. The split is 174 legacy quadrats (Family A) + 56
modern quadrats (Family B), matching the guide's 174 for legacy files.

### 4.2 Does the sample table's flag column agree with the flag file?

Splits combined flags apart on both sides and compares the counts per
flag type.

```{r}
#| label: flag-agreement
full_join(
  opihi_samples |> filter(!is.na(sample_flag)) |>
    separate_longer_delim(sample_flag, ";") |> count(flag = sample_flag),
  opihi_qc_flags |> filter(level == "sample") |>
    separate_longer_delim(flag, ";") |> count(flag),
  by = "flag", suffix = c("_samples", "_qcflags")) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

**Result:** identical counts for all five sample flag types.

### 4.3 Survey-level flags

Survey flags refer to surveys by a text key (file\|date\|site), which
matches the survey table's `src_key` column.

```{r}
#| label: survey-flags
survey_refs <- opihi_qc_flags |> filter(level == "survey") |> pull(ref)
sum(survey_refs %in% opihi_surveys$src_key)    # expect 57 of 57

# the 12 survey flags other than placeholder times
opihi_qc_flags |>
  filter(level == "survey", flag != "placeholder_time_removed") |>
  arrange(flag) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

- `time_assumed_pm` (5): unlabelled times such as 01:05 read as
  afternoon, consistent with the low tide.
- `no_site_or_date_in_file` (2): the 2023 and 2025 classroom files (Part
  3).
- `no_metadata_match` (1): its detail ("matched … within 7 days") is
  identical to `metadata_date_mismatch`, so the flag name contradicts
  its own detail.
- `site_corrected_by_coordinates` (3): large jumps (180–363 km), checked
  in 4.4.

### 4.4 The three site corrections

Shows the three surveys whose site was relabelled to match their
coordinates.

```{r}
#| label: site-corrected
opihi_qc_flags |>
  filter(level == "survey", flag == "site_corrected_by_coordinates") |>
  left_join(opihi_surveys, by = c("ref" = "src_key")) |>
  select(survey_id, source_file, date, site_name, island, n_samples, detail) |>
  print(width = Inf)
```

The "(0.00 km)" in each detail shows the coordinates sit exactly on a
reference point, so they were copied from a site list rather than
measured; either the label or the coordinates could be wrong. Before
using the teacher as evidence, this tests whether teachers keep to one
island:

```{r}
#| label: teacher-islands
# how many islands does each teacher survey?
opihi_surveys |>
  filter(!is.na(teacher_id)) |>
  group_by(teacher_id) |>
  summarise(n_islands = n_distinct(island)) |>
  count(n_islands, name = "n_teachers")

# the teachers of the three flagged surveys, and where else they surveyed
flagged_ids <- c("S0143", "S0167", "S0210")
opihi_surveys |>
  filter(teacher_id %in% teacher_id[survey_id %in% flagged_ids]) |>
  count(teacher_id, island, site_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

65 of 69 teachers survey one island. S0143's teacher only has Hawaii
surveys, supporting master's site. S0167 and S0210 belong to T043, which
appears on five islands (likely a shared or placeholder ID), so the
teacher cannot decide those.

*Manual check of the raw blocks:* each legacy block has its location in
the header and the totals row, with coordinates typed in the block.

| Survey | Block's own location | Coordinates | Master's site |
|------------------|-------------------|------------------|------------------|
| S0210 (2019-05-02) | Kamaole (header and totals row) | typed in block | Kamaole Beach Park ✓ |
| S0167 (2019-01-20) | Diamond Head/Leahi | typed in block | Leahi ✓ |
| S0143 (2018) | Onekahakaha | about 19, −155 (Hawaii) | Onekahakaha ✓ |

**Result:** master's site is correct for all three. The "labelled as"
site in each flag is the location of the **neighbouring** block, so the
legacy parser read the label from the block next door and the coordinate
rule restored the right site. Part 8.1 checks every legacy survey for
the same problem.

### 4.5 Placeholder times

Checks the 45 surveys whose times were removed as template placeholders.

```{r}
#| label: placeholder-times
pt <- opihi_qc_flags |>
  filter(level == "survey", flag == "placeholder_time_removed") |>
  left_join(opihi_surveys, by = c("ref" = "src_key"))

pt |> count(detail)                       # all "start 0.0 stop 0.0417" (00:00-01:00)
pt |> summarise(n = n(), start_blank = sum(is.na(start_time)), stop_blank = sum(is.na(stop_time)))
pt |> count(source_file, sort = TRUE)
```

**Result:** all 45 were the 00:00–01:00 template default (Excel stores
1:00 as 1/24 = 0.0417), and all 45 are now blank. 43 are in the
2004–2008 files.

# Part 6 · Exclusions log

Checks that the 427 records left out of master contain no real data,
except where documented.

```{r}
#| label: exclusions-overview
opihi_exclusions_log |> count(level, reason, sort = TRUE)     # 427 in total
```

### 6.1 The 107 Longitudinal `no_taxon_data` rows and the 6 invalid names

*Manual check of the 2026 Longitudinal file:* column BF has no species
header and a stray "3" where the name should be (the 6
`invalid_taxon_name` cells). Rows 97–266 are template rows with date or
location only and no counts. The Mauliola transect and metadata rows
have recorders, date and location but no organisms.

**Result:** the six "3.0" exclusions are a data-entry problem in the
sheet, not lost data. The 107 rows belong to an unfilled session
(2026-01-25; survey S0247 holds its 26 entered quadrats). A quadrat with
a location but no organisms means "not recorded" rather than a true
zero, which master cannot represent.

### 6.2 The 309 blank template rows and the 2 other `no_taxon_data` rows

Looks up each excluded row on the counts tab of its raw file and checks
for any value above zero in a column that master reads taxon counts
from.

```{r}
#| label: blank-rows
# raw row number of each blank template row (source_ref is "file|r0627")
bl <- opihi_exclusions_log |>
  filter(reason == "blank_template_row") |>
  mutate(src_file = source_file, row = as.integer(str_extract(source_ref, "(?<=\\|r)\\d+")))
anyNA(bl$row)    # expect FALSE

# taxon columns of those files, on the counts tab only
taxon_cols <- master_src |> filter(src_file %in% unique(bl$src_file)) |> distinct(src_file, src_col)
counts_tab <- raw_cells |>
  filter(str_detect(sheet, regex("pt\\s*counts", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  semi_join(taxon_cols, by = c("src_file", "col" = "src_col"))

bl |> inner_join(counts_tab, by = c("src_file", "row")) |>
  filter(data_type == "numeric", numeric > 0) |> nrow()     # counts on excluded rows: expect 0

# the 2 no_taxon_data rows outside the Longitudinal file
two <- opihi_exclusions_log |>
  filter(reason == "no_taxon_data", !str_detect(source_file, "Longitudinal")) |>
  mutate(src_file = source_file, row = as.integer(str_extract(source_ref, "(?<=\\|r)\\d+")))
taxon_cols2 <- master_src |> filter(src_file %in% two$src_file) |> distinct(src_file, src_col)

raw_cells |>
  filter(str_detect(sheet, regex("pt\\s*counts", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  inner_join(two |> select(src_file, row), by = c("src_file", "row")) |>
  semi_join(taxon_cols2, by = c("src_file", "col" = "src_col")) |>
  count(src_file, data_type, has_count = coalesce(numeric, 0) > 0)   # expect no rows
```

**Result:** none of the 309 blank rows or the 2 other rows has a count
in a taxon column.

### 6.3 The excluded 2020 block (block08)

Lists the 2020 blocks that are in master, to see whether block08's
position gives its date.

```{r}
#| label: block08
opihi_surveys |>
  filter(source_file == "OPIHI data 2020.xlsx") |>
  mutate(block = str_match(src_key, "\\|(block\\d+)")[, 2]) |>
  select(block, date, site_name, island, n_samples) |>
  arrange(block)
```

*Manual check:* block08 has species counts (4 taxa, 20 quadrats across
transects 1, 2, 4 and 5, 38 detections) but only "?" placeholders for
site and date.

Blocks run from newest (block01, March) to oldest (block07, January), so

## Part 7 · Taxon names

Checks how raw taxon spellings were mapped to clean names, starting with
the misspellings in S0251.

```{r}
#| label: s0251-names
master_completed |>
  filter(survey_id == "S0251") |>
  distinct(taxon_raw, taxon_clean, analysis_taxon, category) |>
  arrange(taxon_clean) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

Every misspelling in S0251 (for example Turbinania, Caiclmus, Byropsis)
maps to the right species. `opihi_unmatched_names` is empty because the
crosswalk was built from the same data it was applied to, so it can only
catch new spellings. Two mappings need correcting: "unknown Fish" is
categorised as Invertebrate, and the raw spellings of *Dendropoma* were
all mapped to "gregaria".

```{r}
#| label: fish-dendropoma
master_completed |>
  filter(str_detect(taxon_clean, regex("fish|gregari", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  count(taxon_raw, taxon_clean, category, name = "n_rows")
```

The three *Dendropoma* spellings (172 + 10 + 33 rows) correctly become
one taxon; only the label changes. **Decisions:** use the accepted
spelling *Dendropoma gregarium*, and add a Vertebrate category for the
fish.

```{r}
#| label: fix-names
n_before <- nrow(master_completed)

master_completed <- master_completed |>
  mutate(
    across(c(taxon_clean, analysis_taxon),
           ~ if_else(.x == "Dendropoma gregaria", "Dendropoma gregarium", .x)),
    category = if_else(coalesce(taxon_clean == "Unknown fish", FALSE), "Vertebrate", category))

nrow(master_completed) == n_before    # TRUE: no rows added or lost
master_completed |>
  filter(str_detect(taxon_clean, regex("fish|gregari", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  count(taxon_raw, taxon_clean, analysis_taxon, category, name = "n_rows")

change_log <- change_log |>
  add_row(change = "taxon 'Dendropoma gregaria' -> 'Dendropoma gregarium'",
          rows = sum(master_completed$taxon_clean == "Dendropoma gregarium", na.rm = TRUE),
          reason = "accepted spelling; the AI used the majority raw spelling") |>
  add_row(change = "category of 'Unknown fish': Invertebrate -> Vertebrate", rows = 1,
          reason = "fish are vertebrates; the category list had no vertebrate option")
```

### 7.1 One taxon per sample

When several raw spellings become one clean name, two of them can appear
in the same sample. This finds any taxon recorded more than once in a
sample.

```{r}
#| label: duplicates
dups <- master_completed |>
  count(sample_id, taxon_clean, name = "n_rows") |>
  filter(n_rows > 1)
dups    # 2: Sargassum aquifolium and Turbinaria ornata, both in S0251-003

master_completed |>
  semi_join(dups, by = c("sample_id", "taxon_clean")) |>
  select(sample_id, taxon_raw, taxon_clean, count, source_cell)
```

*Manual check:* the raw sheet has two separate lines for each taxon, one
misspelled and one correct. **Decision:** sum each pair into one row,
keeping both raw spellings and both source cells.

```{r}
#| label: merge-duplicates
cols_before  <- names(master_completed)
total_before <- sum(master_completed$count, na.rm = TRUE)
dup_keys     <- dups |> select(sample_id, taxon_clean)

# one row per pair: counts summed, raw spellings and source cells combined
merged <- master_completed |>
  semi_join(dup_keys, by = c("sample_id", "taxon_clean")) |>
  group_by(across(-c(taxon_raw, count, source_cell))) |>
  summarise(taxon_raw   = paste(taxon_raw, collapse = "; "),
            source_cell = paste(source_cell, collapse = "; "),
            count       = sum(count), .groups = "drop")
nrow(merged)    # expect 2

# replace the four rows with the two merged rows
master_completed <- master_completed |>
  anti_join(dup_keys, by = c("sample_id", "taxon_clean")) |>
  bind_rows(merged) |>
  select(all_of(cols_before))

nrow(master_completed)                                      # 22,586
sum(master_completed$count, na.rm = TRUE) == total_before   # TRUE: no count lost
master_completed |> count(sample_id, taxon_clean) |> filter(n > 1) |> nrow()   # 0

change_log <- change_log |> add_row(
  change = "merged duplicate taxon rows in S0251-003 (Sargassum aquifolium 1+2 = 3, Turbinaria ornata 1+1 = 2)",
  rows = 2,
  reason = "typo and correct spelling entered on separate sheet lines (confirmed in raw file); counts summed, both source cells kept")
```

The sheet's own totals for *Turbinaria* add up all groups on a tab,
while master stores each group as its own sample. Summing master by tab
and spelling should reproduce the sheet totals:

```{r}
#| label: turbinaria-totals
master_src |>
  filter(taxon_clean == "Turbinaria ornata", str_detect(src_sheet, "P1")) |>
  group_by(src_file, src_sheet, survey_id, taxon_raw) |>
  summarise(n_samples = n(), total = sum(count), .groups = "drop")
```

**Result:** 2023 P1 = 4 (Turbinania) + 22 (Turbinaria) and 2025 P1 = 6,
matching the sheet totals. Master holds every count; the merge only
joins the two lines within S0251-003.

### 8.1 Is every legacy survey filed under the site written in its own block?

Tests whether the neighbouring-block parser problem found in 4.4 put any
survey at the wrong site. A block's location is written at its first
data column (totals row) and two columns to the right (header), so a
block owns every column from its first data column up to the start of
the next block. This was calibrated on S0210 and S0211, whose cells were
checked by hand.

The code finds every site name written in each legacy file, keeps the
ones inside each survey's own block, and compares them with master's
site. English names (Sand Island, Barbers Point, Diamond Head) and the
ʻokina are handled.

```{r}
#| label: block-location-check
# site names and the text that identifies them in the raw sheets
# (ʻokina and apostrophes are removed before matching)
site_lookup <- tribble(~site_name, ~pattern,
  "Hilo Yacht Club","hilo yacht", "Holoholokai","holoholokai", "Kahaluu Bay","kahaluu",
  "Kaupo","kaupo", "Keei","keei", "Keiki Ponds","keiki pond", "Kiholo Bay","kiholo",
  "Kona Bay Estates","kona bay", "Old Airport","old airport", "Onekahakaha","onekahakaha",
  "Oneo Bay","oneo", "Punaluu Beach Park","punaluu", "Richardsons","richardson",
  "Waiopae","waiopae", "Wawaloli","wawaloli", "Fuji","fuji", "Mahaulepu","mahaulepu",
  "Nukolii","nukolii", "Salt Pond","salt pond", "Waipouli","waipouli", "Hulopoe Bay","hulopoe",
  "Kamaole Beach Park","kamaole", "Keawakapu","keawakapu", "Napili Bay","napili",
  "Waipuilani","waipuilani", "Kapukahehu","kapukahehu", "Mapulehu","mapulehu",
  "Moomomi","moomomi", "Morris Point","morris", "Baby Makapuu","makapuu",
  "Ewa","\\bewa\\b", "Kahana Bay","kahana", "Kalaeloa","kalaeloa|barbers? ?point",
  "Keiki Bay","keiki bay", "Lanikai Point","lanikai", "Leahi","leahi|diamond head",
  "Maili Beach","maili", "Mauliola","mauliola|sand island", "Mokauea Island","mokauea",
  "Sandy Beach","sandy", "Turtle Bay","turtle bay", "Waianae High School Reef","waianae")

# legacy (block-based) surveys
legacy <- surveys_completed |>
  filter(str_detect(src_key, "\\|block")) |>
  select(survey_id, source_file, date, site_name)

# the columns each block owns: its first data column up to the next block's start
spans <- master_src |>
  semi_join(legacy, by = "survey_id") |>
  group_by(survey_id, src_file) |>
  summarise(min_col = min(src_col), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(src_file) |> arrange(min_col, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(end_col = lead(as.numeric(min_col), default = Inf) - 1) |> ungroup()

# legacy files with more than one tab would need extra care: expect 0 rows
raw_cells |> filter(src_file %in% spans$src_file) |>
  distinct(src_file, sheet) |> count(src_file) |> filter(n > 1)

# every cell in the legacy files that names a site
site_cells <- raw_cells |>
  filter(src_file %in% spans$src_file, data_type == "character") |>
  mutate(txt = tolower(character) |> str_remove_all("['ʻ‘’`]"))

site_hits <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(site_lookup)), \(i)
  site_cells |> filter(str_detect(txt, site_lookup$pattern[i])) |>
    transmute(src_file, row, col, label_site = site_lookup$site_name[i]))

# site names found inside each survey's own block
own <- site_hits |>
  inner_join(spans, by = "src_file", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(col >= min_col, col <= end_col) |>
  group_by(survey_id) |>
  summarise(labels = paste(sort(unique(label_site)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")

# compare with master's site
block_check <- legacy |>
  left_join(own, by = "survey_id") |>
  mutate(status = case_when(
    is.na(labels) ~ "no label found",
    map2_lgl(site_name, coalesce(labels, ""), \(s, l) s %in% str_split_1(l, ", ")) ~ "match",
    TRUE ~ "different"))

block_check |> count(status)    # expect 227 match
block_check |> filter(status != "match")
```

**Result:** all 227 legacy surveys are filed under the site written in
their own block. The parser problem only changed the wording of the
three flags in 4.4; it never placed a survey at the wrong site.

```{r}
opihi_qc_flags |>
```

All 10 `total_points_mismatch` flags are in the 2024 datasheet. This
compares the typed "Total Points" with the sum of the cells, and shows
the two inferred samples next to their neighbours.

```{r}
#| label: flag-details-check
# 1. total_points_mismatch: typed "Total Points" in the 2024 sheet vs the sum of the cells
pts <- xlsx_cells(file.path(raw_dir, "OPIHI 2024 datasheet .xlsx")) |>
  filter(str_detect(sheet, regex("pt\\s*counts", ignore_case = TRUE)))

tp_col <- pts |>
  filter(str_detect(character, regex("^\\s*total\\s*points", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  distinct(col) |> pull(col)
tp_col    # two matches (95 and 68); column 95 holds the quadrat totals

opihi_qc_flags |>
  filter(str_detect(flag, "total_points_mismatch")) |>
  mutate(row = as.integer(str_extract(detail, "(?<=\\|r)\\d+"))) |>
  left_join(pts |> filter(col == tp_col[1]) |> select(row, typed_total = numeric), by = "row") |>
  left_join(opihi_samples |> select(sample_id, point_sum, points_possible), by = c("ref" = "sample_id")) |>
  mutate(difference = typed_total - point_sum) |>
  select(ref, row, typed_total, point_sum, points_possible, difference)

# 2. the two "inferred" samples next to their neighbours
opihi_samples |>
  filter(sample_id %in% c("S0246-036", "S0246-037", "S0246-038",
                          "S0128-010", "S0128-011", "S0128-012")) |>
  select(sample_id, transect, quadrat, point_m, point_sum, sample_flag)
```

In 5 samples the cells add up to exactly 25 while the typed total is
wrong; in 4 the cells exceed 25 (these are also flagged over 25); in 1
they add up to 18. The typed totals are the unreliable part. The two
inferred samples fit between their neighbours.

| Flag | n | Evidence | Decision |
|-----------------|-----------------|----------------------|-----------------|
| `points_over_25` | 230 | Rule recomputed exactly; 174 legacy + 56 modern | **Keep, flagged.** Fine for detection; exclude or note for percent cover |
| `total_points_mismatch` | 10 | 5 sum to 25 with wrong typed totals; 4 over 25; 1 sums to 18 | **Keep the cell values** |
| `placeholder_time_removed` | 45 | All 00:00–01:00 template; all blank | **Fix (applied by the AI)** |
| `site_corrected_by_coordinates` | 3 | Raw blocks checked; 227 of 227 legacy sites match | **Keep** master's site; flag text is wrong |
| `time_assumed_pm` | 5 | Fits the low tide times | **Keep** |
| `no_site_or_date_in_file` | 2 | S0251 recovered; S0252 not recoverable | **Fix S0251 (done); keep S0252**, excluded from site/time analyses |
| `metadata_date_mismatch` | 1 | Matched within 7 days; data-row date kept | **Keep** |
| `no_metadata_match` | 1 | Detail says it did match | **Keep**; flag name is wrong |
| `date_inferred` | 1 | S0246-037 fits its neighbours | **Keep** |
| `header_inferred` | 1 | S0128-011 = T2 Q1, between T1 Q10 and T2 Q2 | **Keep** |
| `group_label_mismatch` | 1 | In S0252, which has no site | **Keep** |

# 3rd Script: Functions

This script creates four functions that can be reused to explore the
OPIHI monitoring dataset. These functions help understand how many
different taxa were recorded at each site, how/if taxon richness varies
across sampling years, and where and when were specifc taxa observed in
the dataset.

## Writing Function 1 - How Many Different Taxa are Recorded at Each Site

```{r}
TaxonRichness <- function(data) {

  result <- data |>
    filter(!is.na(site_name)) |>
    group_by(site_name) |>
    summarise(
      richness = n_distinct(analysis_taxon, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  return(result)
}
```

This function calculates the number of different taxa recorded at each
sampling site. AI was utilized to get this function.

**Input:** data = the cleaned OPIHI master sheet that contains the site
names(site_name) and the taxon IDs (analysis_taxon).

**Output:** Dataframe with two columns: site_name and richness, which
provided the number of unique taxa recorded at each site.

### Testing Function 1

```{r}
SiteRichness <- TaxonRichness(opihi_master)
```

## Writing Function 2 - Taxon Richness for Each Site During Each Year

```{r}
TaxonRichnessYear <- function(data) {

  result <- data |>
    filter(!is.na(site_name), !is.na(year)) |>
    group_by(site_name, year) |>
    summarise(
      richness = n_distinct(analysis_taxon, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(site_name, year)

  return(result)
}
```

This function is similar to Function 1, calculates richness for each
site during each sampling year.

**Input:** data = the cleaned OPIHI master sheet that contains the site
names(site_name), year, and the taxon IDs (analysis_taxon).

**Output:** The dataframe containing site_name, year, and richness,
which shows the number of unique taxa recorded at each site during each
year.

### Test Function 2

```{r}
TaxonRichnessYearResults <- TaxonRichnessYear(opihi_master)

```

```{r}
unique(opihi_master$taxon_clean)
```

Before creating Function 3, I wanted to included all the different taxon
names available in our cleaned dataset for the viewer to see.

## Writing Function 3 - Specific Taxon at A Certain Site and Year

```{r}
FindTaxon <- function(data, taxon, site, sampling_year = NULL) {

  result <- data |>
    filter(
      taxon_clean == taxon,
      site_name == site
    )

  if (!is.null(sampling_year)) {
    result <- result |>
      filter(year == sampling_year)
  }

  return(result)
}
```

Function 3 allows you to search the cleaned data for a particular taxon
at a sampling site.

**Input:** data = the cleaned OPIHI dataset, taxon = the name of the
taxon we want to find, site = the sample site, sampling year = if no
year is provided, the function includes all years available

**Output:** A dataframe showing all the records of the selected taxon at
a specific site, and year if one is chosen.

### Test Function 3

```{r}
FindTaxon(opihi_master, "Sargassum spp.", "Kahana Bay")

FindTaxon(opihi_master, "Sargassum spp.", "Leahi")
```

Two examples of how function 3 can be used, for example with *Sargassum*
spp.

## Writing Function 4 - How Many Sites Recorded a Particular Taxon Each Year

```{r}
TaxonByYear <- function(data, taxon) {

  result <- data |>
    filter(taxon_clean == taxon) |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(
      number_sites = n_distinct(site_name, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(year)

  return(result)
}
```

Our fourth function calculates the number of different sampling sites
where a particular taxon was recorded during each year. This can be
useful for exploring the distribution of taxa over time and comparing
where different species have been observed in the dataset.

**Input:** data = the cleaned OPIHI dataset, and taxon = the name of the
taxon you want to investigate.

**Output:** A tibble with two columns: year and number_sites, showing
how many unique sampling sites recorded the selected taxon during each
year.

### Testing Function 4

```{r}
TaxonByYear(opihi_master, "Dictyosphaeria versluysii")

TaxonByYear(opihi_master, "Diadema paucispinum")
```

Here are two examples of how you can use function 4 for research.

## Organizing data

```{r}
# only the algae data
algae <- raw |>
  filter(category == "Algae", island=="Oahu") |>
  left_join(lookup, by = "taxon_clean") |>
  mutate(origin_group = case_when(
    origin_status %in% c("Native", "Native (likely)")             ~ "Native",
    origin_status %in% c("Non-native", "Non-native (invasive)")   ~ "Non-native",
    TRUE ~ "Unresolved"   # cryptogenic, genus-level, turf, unknown groups
  ))

# Every quadrat surveyed on Oahu (so quadrats with no algae count as 0)
samples <- raw |>
  filter(sample_type == "quadrat", island == "Oahu") |>
  distinct(sample_id, site_name, year, lat = latitude, lon = longitude, points_possible)

# Algae points per quadrat
algae_pts <- raw |>
  filter(category == "Algae", sample_type == "quadrat") |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  summarise(points = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Mean % cover per site
site_algae <- samples |>
  left_join(algae_pts, by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(cover = pmin(100 * replace_na(points, 0) / points_possible, 100)) |>
  group_by(site_name, lat, lon) |>
  summarise(mean_cover = mean(cover), n_quadrats = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Algae points per quadrat, split into native vs non-native
group_pts <- raw |>
  filter(category == "Algae", sample_type == "quadrat") |>
  left_join(lookup, by = "taxon_clean") |>
  mutate(origin_group = case_when(
    origin_status %in% c("Native", "Native (likely)")           ~ "Native",
    origin_status %in% c("Non-native", "Non-native (invasive)") ~ "Non-native",
    TRUE ~ "Unresolved")) |>
  filter(origin_group %in% c("Native", "Non-native")) |>
  group_by(sample_id, origin_group) |>
  summarise(points = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

quad <- samples |>
  crossing(origin_group = c("Native", "Non-native")) |>
  left_join(group_pts, by = c("sample_id", "origin_group")) |>
  mutate(cover = pmin(100 * replace_na(points, 0) / points_possible, 100))

# Site level (map circles) and site x year level (popup graphs)
site_group <- quad |>
  group_by(site_name, lat, lon, origin_group) |>
  summarise(mean_cover = mean(cover), n_quadrats = n_distinct(sample_id),
            .groups = "drop")

site_year <- quad |>
  group_by(site_name, year, origin_group) |>
  summarise(mean_cover = mean(cover), n_quadrats = n_distinct(sample_id),
            .groups = "drop")
```
